item.title: Courtly Worlds
item.description: The Tale of Genji — Murasaki Shikibu, early eleventh century. It is primarily a prose narrative, but its characters frequently compose and exchange waka — short thirty-one-syllable poems used for courtship, farewell, veiled criticism, emotional disclosure, and other socially delicate communication.

item.title: Philosophical Poetry
item.description:
On Socrates

Greek Anthology 7.96, attributed to Diogenes Laertius

Drink now, Socrates, in the house of Zeus.
Truly a god called you wise,
and Wisdom herself is divine.
From the Athenians you received only hemlock;
but they drank it themselves through your mouth.

Against the Fear of Death

item.title: Renaissance Art from Perspective to Mannerism
item.description:
Artworks and Images

Early Renaissance: Constructed Perspective

Masaccio and Uccello both construct pictorial space with linear perspective. Masaccio uses it to make the painted chapel appear to continue into the wall; Uccello makes the geometry conspicuous in the lances, fallen weapons, and foreshortened forms.

Perspective: Masaccio and Uccello

1 / 1

Masaccio and Uccello both use perspective to construct pictorial space, but to very different effects.

item.title: The Dutch Golden Age
item.description:

1 / 1
